Job Description

What is the Opportunity?

The Associate Director, Market Risk (FRTB Capital) will play a pivotal role in building and leading RBC’s market risk regulatory reporting infrastructure under the Basel 3 Endgame (B3EG) framework. The individual will architect end-to-end production of critical US IHC regulatory submission including the FFIEC 102 (weekly FRTB capital reporting), FR Y-9C Risk-to-Finance reconciliations, and CCAR Market RWA projections for FRY-14A. This high-impact role offers ownership over establishing automated reporting workflows, partnering with IT on system implementations and data pipeline enhancements, and driving strategic initiatives such as FRTB calculator improvements and IMA vs. SA approach analysis. The ideal candidate brings 5+ years of market risk reporting or regulatory capital experience, strong technical capabilities in Python and SQL, and a track record of delivering accurate regulatory submissions in production environments.

What will you do?

Lead the design, implementation, and ongoing production of Market Risk regulatory reports under B3EG, including the FFIEC 102 and weekly FRTB capital reports and CCAR Market RWA 9-quarter projections; establish automated reporting views and dashboards to support granular schedule-level reporting – 25%.
Partner with IT and Group risk Analytics team on FRTB Standardized Approach (SA) calculator enhancements for jurisdictional changes, system implementations, and data pipeline automation; coordinate UAT testing, production validation and reporting infrastructure improvements – 20%
.
Build and maintain the Risk-to-Finance reconciliation framework (FR Y-9C), perform comprehensive data analysis across market risk exposures, capital calculations, and reporting datasets; including root-cause analysis of breaks and develop automated reconciliation tools and validation checks– 20%.
Design and implement controls automation solutions for reporting and capital calculation processes; build automated validation checks, exception monitoring tools, and alerting mechanisms to enhance data quality, control effectiveness, and reduce manual intervention – 15%.

Develop and maintain reporting documentation including data lineage, process flows, line-item mapping, and methodology descriptions; monitor regulatory developments, participate in FRB data collection exercises (e.g., HPE/QIS), and support internal audit, RCSA, and regulatory examination processes – 10%.

What do you need to succeed?

Hands-on experience with Business Intelligence and reporting tools (Tableau, OBI, or equivalent) and market risk systems; ability to translate data into actional insights through dashboard and visualizations.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills with demonstrated ability to synthesize complex regulatory and technical concepts for senior management and regulators, and cross-functional stakeholders.
Ability to manage recurring production processes under tight weekly deadlines while maintaining accuracy and completeness.
Autonomous, highly motivated, and able to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.

About Us

Legora is redefining how legal work gets done. Not built for lawyers, built with them. We work alongside the world’s best legal teams, who expect excellence, precision, and speed, and we hold ourselves to the same bar.

Our AI-native workspace lets legal professionals move faster, think more clearly, and operate with sharper precision. By analysing thousands of documents in minutes and powering end-to-end workflows, we cut through complexity, teams can focus on what matters: judgment, strategy, and outcomes.

2,100+ customers across 80+ countries trust us, including Cleary Gottlieb, Goodwin, Linklaters, White & Case, Dentons, and Barclays. We’ve scaled to $200M+ in ARR
, with teams across Europe, North America and APAC, and continue to expand through acquisitions including Qura, Walter AI, Graceview, Cadastral, and Wexler.

We partner with world-class performers: including Aaron Judge and the New York Yankees, Ludvig Åberg (and his caddie), and campaigns featuring Jude Law.

Joining Legora means three things.

We lean in: ownership over titles, outcomes over intentions.
We fight for excellence: high standards, direct, ego-free feedback.
We grow together: as a team and with our customers.

Mission before ego. Everyone contributes. No one coasts.

If you’re driven by impact, pace, and raising the bar. This is the place.

The Role

Let's get the tricky part out of the way. Legal Engineering does not fit neatly into a traditional box. It combines legal practice, product fluency, enterprise change, commercial judgment and client leadership.

As Director, Legal Engineering, your mission is to make Legal Engineering the commercial and delivery engine for Canada, anchored in our Toronto office. Reporting to the Head of Legal Engineering, North America, you will set the craft bar, build the Canadian team and its Team Lead layer, partner closely with Go-to-Market and Engagement, lead selectively on the highest-stakes clients, and turn local learning into playbooks that scale across the Canadian market.

This is a Director-level leadership role. Your primary output will be the quality and performance of the team and system you build. You will stay close enough to the product and the work to coach credibly, while moving your own time toward hiring, leadership development, senior relationships, market strategy and cross-functional execution.

You will have the autonomy to shape how Legal Engineering runs in a strategically important market, together with the responsibility to keep that model connected to Legora's North American and global standards.

What You'll Do

Lead the Legal Engineering function for Canada from the Toronto office, including its operating rhythm, quality bar, capacity model and local partnership with Go-to-Market and Engagement.
Hire exceptional Legal Engineers and future leaders. Own the quality bar from sourcing and interview calibration through closing, onboarding and ramp.
Build a manager layer of Team Leads who each own and develop a group of Legal Engineers. Delegate real decision rights and create clear succession paths so the function becomes stronger and less dependent on you over time.
Give direct, evidence-based feedback. Coach hard, set clear expectations and act decisively when the performance or values bar is not met.
Partner with Canadian commercial leadership on priority accounts, pilots, rollouts and escalations. Connect Legal Engineering activity to conversion, adoption, usage, expansion and revenue.
Act as the lead legal architect on selected enterprise engagements. Translate a real legal problem into a concrete Legora workflow, then turn successful delivery into a reusable playbook others can run.
Oversee complex, multi-stakeholder programs with clear governance, owners, outcomes, leading indicators and risk management.
Build trusted relationships with Managing Partners, General Counsels, Heads of Innovation, Legal Operations leaders and other senior stakeholders.
Represent the market's voice inside Legora. Translate recurring client patterns and product gaps into clear, actionable input for Product.
Shape Legora's point of view on AI and legal work in Canada. Contribute through executive client forums, events, writing and practical market insight grounded in first-hand work.
Create clean handoffs across Go-to-Market, Legal Engineering and Engagement so that commercial momentum, delivery quality and long-term adoption reinforce one another.

How You Lead

Strong leadership in this role looks like this:

Hiring judgment and partnership. You treat hiring as company-building work. You own open seats end to end, partner closely with Talent and keep the bar high when growth pressure rises.
Talent development and accountability. Your team knows where they stand. Feedback is early, written and specific. You create stretch, develop future leaders and distinguish coachable gaps from persistent underperformance.
Ownership, delegation and operating rhythm. You own the market outcome while giving others real authority. Priorities, decision rights, leading indicators and dependencies are clear. The team runs well without you in every room.
Team-first leadership and culture. You give the team credit, absorb accountability for misses and create enough trust that bad news travels early. People grow faster because they worked for you.
Performance bar and decisive judgment. You protect the standard with speed, fairness and evidence. Strong performers trust you to address mediocrity, and difficult decisions remain humane and unambiguous.
The practical test is simple: the Canadian team should produce better work, stronger leaders and more repeatable customer outcomes because of the system you built, not because you personally carried every important engagement.

What You Bring

You may come from a leading law firm, an in-house legal function, legal operations, legal innovation, professional services, legal technology, or a combination of those worlds. The common thread is that you have moved beyond advising on change and have built the people, systems and client outcomes that make change real.

You Will Thrive In This Role If You:

You may come from a leading law firm, an in-house legal function, legal operations, legal innovation, professional services, legal technology, or a combination of those worlds. The common thread is that you have moved beyond advising on change and have built the people, systems and client outcomes that make change real.

You Will Thrive In This Role If You:

Are a qualified lawyer, licensed (or eligible to be licensed) in Ontario or another Canadian jurisdiction, with substantial legal, legal-operations or legal-technology experience, and a strong understanding of how sophisticated law firms and in-house legal teams make decisions.

Are deeply curious about generative AI and product. You do not need to be a software engineer, but you must be able to learn the platform, challenge use-case design and coach credible client work.
Can hold your own with a Managing Partner, General Counsel or executive team while remaining practical with the people doing the work.
Understand the commercial realities of legal services and enterprise software. You can connect Legal Engineering to pipeline, client value, adoption, usage and revenue.
Bring structure to ambiguity without creating process for its own sake. You build operating systems that improve speed and quality.
Have strong hiring and performance judgment. You can attract high-calibre people, develop them directly and protect the standard when a seat is not working.
Communicate fluently in English, in writing and in person. French is a strong plus.
Are based in the Greater Toronto Area and able to work from our Toronto office five days per week, with travel across Canada for strategic clients, market development and team leadership.

What’s In It For You

Global collaboration: Partner with teams and clients domestic and internationally.

jobs.description:
About Cheaper Inference Cheaper Inference is a drop-in, OpenAI-compatible API that charges developers about 30% below provider list price
. We save money in two ways:
Marketplace pricing.
Providers with spare LLM capacity compete on price. We send each request to the cheapest healthy offer and pass the discount on to customers.
Fewer wasted tokens.
Our optimization pipeline uses current research to cut tokens from each request. Every customer can see exactly what each request saved.

Our customers are developers and technical teams running production workloads through our API. When something goes wrong, such as a failed request, a surprising bill or a confusing savings number, they need fast, accurate, technically credible help. Support is part of the product.

The role You'll build and lead customer support at Cheaper Inference from the ground up. You'll handle tickets yourself at first, then design the systems, tools, documentation and team that let support grow with the company. You'll be accountable for how fast we respond, how well we resolve issues, how satisfied customers are and how much of what you learn gets back to the product team.
You'll work closely with the founders and engineering. A large share of our support is technical. You'll often be the first to spot an API issue, a billing edge case or a confusing part of the dashboard.

What you'll do Own the support function.
Set up support channels (email, in-app chat, Discord or Slack communities), choose and configure the tools, and define SLAs, priority levels and escalation paths.
Handle tickets directly at first.
Answer technical questions about API integration, streaming, rate limits, errors, model availability, request headers, prompt A/B experiments and billing.
Run incident communication.
Work with engineering during outages or slowdowns. Post updates on the status page, let affected customers know proactively and follow up after incidents.
Build self-serve help.
Create and maintain help center articles, troubleshooting guides, FAQs and macros so customers can solve common problems themselves. Work with the docs team to fill gaps.
Handle billing and account issues.
Resolve questions about usage, invoices, credits, refunds, savings attribution and plan changes accurately and fairly.
Get customer feedback to the product team.
Tag and analyze tickets to find recurring problems, bugs and feature requests. Report clear, prioritized findings to product and engineering.
Use automation wisely.
Set up AI-assisted support (triage, suggested replies, a documentation chatbot) where it helps, without letting quality slip.
Hire and grow the team.
Decide when and who to hire, including support engineers and specialists. Build the onboarding, training and quality review processes they'll need.
Measure everything.
Track first response time, time to resolution, CSAT, ticket volume per customer and the share of issues customers solve on their own. Report on these regularly and keep improving them.
Support key accounts.
Work with sales and success on onboarding, migrations and dedicated support for high-value customers.

What success looks like First 90 days:
Support tools, SLAs and escalation paths in place. A core help center live. Response times and CSAT measured and improving. A regular report of customer feedback going to product.
First year:
A support operation that can grow, with a strong self-serve rate, consistently high CSAT, a clear plan for hiring the team and measurable product improvements driven by support findings.

What we're looking for 4+ years
in customer support or support engineering, including at least 1–2 years leading support or building it from scratch, ideally at an API, developer tool, infrastructure or SaaS company.
Strong technical skills. You're comfortable reading API docs, testing requests with curl or Postman, reading logs and error codes, and talking with engineers in their terms.
Experience with support platforms (e.g., Zendesk, Intercom, Plain, Front, Help Scout) and status page tools.
Excellent writing. Your replies are clear, empathetic and accurate, and your documentation actually gets used.
Experience handling billing and usage-based pricing questions.
Calm judgment during incidents and escalations.
A data-driven approach to support metrics and process improvement.
An owner's mindset and comfort doing the work yourself at an early-stage company.

Nice to have Experience with LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic or similar) or AI infrastructure products.
Basic scripting or SQL to investigate issues without waiting for engineering.
Experience running developer communities on Discord or Slack.
Experience setting up AI-assisted support workflows.

Job Summary

The Senior Director, Integrated Talent Solutions (ITS), is responsible for leading the integrated Talent Plan and global ITS delivery for Global Operations and Global Markets. This role translates business priorities into talent strategies that build critical capabilities, strengthen leadership pipelines and support business growth.

As the strategic and systems partner to the Functional People Team (FPT) leader, the Senior Director connects the talent engine across executive hiring, early career, succession, internal mobility, development and recruiting. The role partners with business executives, HR Business Partners, Organizational Effectiveness and HR Centers of Excellence to shape skills-based solutions across build, buy, borrow and bot.

This leader directly manages the Director responsible for AMERS talent delivery and the EMEA and APAC business-line leads. Global Operations represents the larger hiring footprint, with support for Global Markets aligned to its specific business and talent priorities.

Serve as a trusted advisor to the FPT leader and business executives on talent risks, critical capabilities, workforce readiness and leadership needs.
Translate business priorities into an integrated Talent Plan with clear outcomes, ownership and delivery commitments across regions.

Alberta Blue Cross® is an Alberta based organization dedicated to delivering exceptional customer experience and community leadership. We’re committed to providing the best health coverage to over 1.8 million members and take an active role in promoting wellness. Overview

We have an exciting opportunity for a Director, IT Cybersecurity to join our dynamic IT team. Reporting to the Director, CISO, this position is a senior enterprise leader responsible for shaping, governing, and advancing the cybersecurity strategy for Alberta Blue Cross. This role provides authoritative oversight of the cybersecurity portfolio and ensures the organization is equipped with a resilient, risk‑based security posture that protects our systems, data, and reputation. The role ensures that our cybersecurity team continues to be a strong partner for IT and the business, that our cybersecurity practice is optimized, and that we are positioned for rapid response to cybersecurity events and incidents.

A key mandate of this role is to define and execute our cybersecurity strategy, and to continuously evolve our risk-based cybersecurity program to strengthen our organization’s resilience.

What You Will Do

Lead and inspire our cybersecurity teams, fostering a culture of collaboration, accountability and high performance.
Direct and oversee a team of cybersecurity managers and subject matter experts.
Mentor and develop team members to strengthen capability, support growth and build an engaged, high-performing workforce.
Define and execute a multi‑year cybersecurity strategy aligned to enterprise objectives, risk appetite, and regulatory expectations.
Manage and support the continuous assessment of our cybersecurity practice.
Build and maintain strong relationships with senior executives, business leaders, and technology partners to influence decision‑making and embed cybersecurity into enterprise planning.
Establish and maintain strategic external partnerships to strengthen our practice and represent Alberta Blue Cross.
Lead cybersecurity governance to provide effective management of the cybersecurity program and enable risk-based decision making.
Oversee the entire cybersecurity practice to ensure our cybersecurity risk is within the organization’s tolerance levels.
Lead the management and evolution of our cybersecurity policy, standards, runbooks and methodologies.
Ensure compliance to internal and external standards, regulations and audit expectations.
Partner with business leaders and technology teams to ensure alignment, manage dependencies, and drive successful outcomes.
Direct the response to critical and enterprise‑wide cybersecurity incidents, ensuring coordinated action, executive communication, and rapid recovery.

POSITION SCOPE

Strategic alignment with Enterprise Risk, Privacy, Legal, Human Resources, and other key partners to ensure a unified approach to risk and compliance.
Accountability for the IT cybersecurity portfolio, including governance, operations, risk management, and strategic planning.
Drive significant operational impact in delivery performance, prioritization discipline, risk mitigation, and value realization.
Influence senior leadership and executive teams with cybersecurity insights to support strategic decision.
Manage the budget and spend for the entire cybersecurity portfolio.
Oversight of the cybersecurity partner ecosystem, ensuring scalable, resilient, and high‑quality service delivery.

Key Accountabilities

Accountable for the current state and management of the risk associated with IT cybersecurity.
Continuous monitoring of emerging threats, technologies, and regulatory changes to inform strategic investments and roadmap evolution.
Thought leadership in modern cybersecurity practices, advocating for innovation and continuous improvement.
Alignment of cybersecurity initiatives with enterprise risk, privacy, legal, and HR frameworks.
Preparation and delivery of cybersecurity reporting to executive leadership and the Board of Directors.
Leadership of enterprise‑wide incident response, ensuring coordinated action and timely resolution.
Representation of Alberta Blue Cross on national committees and regulatory bodies, strengthening our influence and industry alignment.

KEY SUCCESS MEASURES

Demonstrated reduction and effective management of cybersecurity risk across the organization.
Strong organizational resilience and rapid response to cybersecurity threats and incidents.
Timely closure of audit findings and compliance gaps.
Mature, repeatable, and well‑governed cybersecurity processes.
High confidence in cybersecurity leadership from executives, IT, and business partners.
Clear, well‑defined roles and responsibilities across the cybersecurity organization.
High levels of cybersecurity awareness and engagement across the enterprise.
Measurable improvements in mean time to detect and respond to cybersecurity events.

What You Will Have

Bachelor’s degree in information technology or a related field; advanced education or cybersecurity certifications are strong assets.
10+ years of progressive IT leadership experience, including 5+ years overseeing enterprise cybersecurity portfolios.
Strong knowledge of, and experience with, NIST Cybersecurity Framework.
Strong financial acumen, including budgeting, forecasting, capital planning, and value realization.
Proven ability to build and lead high-performing teams while fostering a culture of collaboration, accountability and trust.
Strong strategic thinking and data-driven decision making skills.
Composure and leadership presence during high intensity and critical cybersecurity events.
Excellent communication and relationship building skills with the ability to influence at all levels, including executives.
Demonstrated change leadership; guiding teams through transformation with resilience, clarity, and empathy.
A forward-looking, innovative, and adaptable mindset with the ability to anticipate organizational needs.
Demonstrated curiosity and commitment to lifelong learning; actively exploring new ideas, asking questions, and seeking knowledge to fuel innovation.
Ability to thrive in dynamic environments, adapt quickly to shifting priorities while guiding others to embrace new ways of working with empathy, patience, and persistence.
Ability to inspire and develop talent; build high performing, engaged teams through coaching, mentoring, and accountability.
Demonstrated strengths in negotiation, budgeting, planning, organizing, and delegation.
Experienced in partnering with senior leaders to shape and deliver strategies that drive measurable results.

Strategic thinking

Proficiency level – Advanced.
Evidence – Demonstrated in portfolio alignment outcomes.

Leadership

Description – Builds high-performing teams and leads change.

Proficiency level – Advanced.
Evidence – Dashboard use, forecasting accuracy.

Proficiency level – Advanced.
Evidence – Cross-functional success cases.

Proficiency level – Advanced.
Evidence – Effective leadership of cybersecurity events.

Strategic thinking:

Consistently anticipates enterprise impacts before decisions are made.
Connect portfolio choices to external market and organizational context.

Leadership:

Model calm, confident leadership during ambiguity.
Actively coach team members and builds successors.

Employ critical thinking leveraging data to challenge assumptions and drive prioritization.
Simplify complex information for executive decision making.

Proactively seek alignment across business functions.
Resolve conflicts by focusing on outcomes, not positions.

Demonstrate effective leadership during highly intense cybersecurity events.
Skilled at managing and leveraging relationships with partner divisions to ensure a coordinated and highly effective response to cybersecurity events.

Are you looking to join an innovative, market-leading company where you can truly elevate your career? At Kinaxis we are serious about culture, we are serious about technology, we are serious about customers, and we are serious about not taking ourselves too seriously. If you are looking to be part of an incredible growth story, then we might just be the place for you!

In 1984, we started out as a team of three engineers. Today, we have grown to become a global organization with over 2000 employees around the world, 6 global office and a best-in-class HQ in Ottawa, Canada. As winners of several Top Employer awards globally, we are proud to work with our customers and employees towards solving some of the biggest challenges facing supply chains today.

Kinaxis is a global leader in modern supply chain orchestration, powering complex global supply chains, and supporting the people who manage them. Our powerful, AI infused platform provides full transparency and visibility across end-to-end supply chains, enabling our customers to make faster, better decisions. We are trusted by renowned global brands to provide the agility and predictability needed to navigate today’s volatility and disruption. With more than 40,000 users in over 100 countries, we are expanding our team as we continue to innovate and revolutionize how we support our customers.

Location

Our headquarters and most of our team are based in Ottawa. For employees located in Ottawa,

this role follows a hybrid work model, with an expectation of approximately four days per week

in the office at our headquarters. We also welcome remote candidates from anywhere in

Canada.

About The Role

The Vice President, Financial Accounting & Reporting is a senior accounting and controllership executive for a global public company. Working in close partnership with the CFO, the VP, Financial Accounting & Reporting ensures the integrity, discipline, and operational effectiveness of the company’s financial management framework across accounting, financial reporting, internal controls, audit oversight, compliance, and revenue accounting globally.

The role serves as a trusted advisor to the CFO and Audit Committee on financial governance, controllership, regulatory readiness, and enterprise risk management related to financial operations and reporting

Vacancy Status

This is an existing job vacancy

Lead the day-to-day operating rhythm of the accounting, external reporting, and internal control functions, with accountability for efficient and accurate close processes, disciplined financial administration, and effective oversight of core accounting operations and global compliance.
Ensure timely, accurate, and decision-useful financial reporting, including external reporting obligations such as OSC and SEC filings and public disclosures, in compliance with IFRS/US GAAP, internal policies, and public-company requirements.
Oversee audit readiness, external audit coordination, control certification support, Canada NI 52-109 requirements, U.S. Sarbanes-Oxley readiness, and the operational processes required to maintain a strong compliance posture across jurisdictions.
Partner with risk management and internal audit.
Support the CFO in Audit Committee matters and serve as a senior operational counterpart on financial governance, controls, and compliance topics.
Ensure accounting processes scale effectively as the business grows in complexity across geographies, products, commercial models, and regulatory obligations.
Grow high-performing teams and create an environment that supports collaboration, operational excellence, and modern enterprise thinking.

What we are looking for

15 years of progressive financial leadership experience.
Significant experience with public-company reporting, external audit, internal controls,

regulatory compliance, and Audit Committee support.

TSX experience is required; NASDAQ and NYSE experience is highly desirable.
Deep knowledge of IFRS, US GAAP, SOX, and internal control frameworks is highly

desirable, including direct experience owning SOX/ICFR programs.

Strong understanding of revenue recognition (IFRS 15/ASC 606) and operational finance

best practices.

Big Four public accounting background, particularly with public-company audit, SEC/OSC
reporting, SOX/ICFR, or complex technology clients.
An active CPA designation is required for this role.
Strong presentation and communication skills at the senior management and board level

#DF-LI1

Our platform directly helps companies power the world’s supply chains. We see the results of what we do out in the world every day, when we see store shelves stocked, when medications are available for our loved ones, and so much more.

Companies across industries trust us to help them take control of their integrated business planning and digital supply chain. Some of our customers include Lockheed Martin, Unilever, P&G, ExxonMobil, Cisco and more.

Position Overview:

At Finning, we're committed to delivering exceptional customer outcomes through safe, efficient, and high-performing operations. We are seeking a strategic and visible leader to join our team as Director, Elk Valley Operations, providing enterprise-wide leadership and accountability.

This leadership role will serve as the single point of contact for the site leadership team, driving collaboration across service, parts, supply chain, training, and operational functions to ensure seamless execution and long-term success. With accountability for salaried and hourly employees, this role requires a strong operational leader who can build high-performing teams, develop future leaders, strengthen customer partnerships, and deliver outstanding safety, financial, and operational results. The successful candidate will maintain a strong field presence, spending a minimum of three days per week at mine sites to support employees, customers, and business objectives.

We anticipate the base salary for this position will be between $160,000 - $170,000 yearly. Actual salary will be based on the candidate's experience. This role is also eligible for Regional Wage Allowance and Short Term Incentive Program.

Job Description:

What You'll Do

Provide strategic and operational leadership for Finning's Elk Valley operations, ensuring alignment across service, parts, supply chain, training, and support functions to achieve business objectives.
Act as the primary relationship owner and trusted advisor for the customer site leadership team, driving operational excellence and contract execution.
Champion a culture of safety excellence by leading health and safety initiatives, ensuring compliance with all regulatory and company requirements, and fostering an incident-free workplace.
Lead, coach, and develop leaders across the region while building a strong succession pipeline and creating opportunities for employee growth and career development.
Oversee regional financial performance, including budgeting, forecasting, contract management, asset optimization, and delivery of revenue and profitability targets.
Drive continuous improvement through the review of key operational metrics related to safety, quality, customer experience, productivity, and cost management.
Partner with labour relations stakeholders to build and maintain positive relationships with unionized employees and union representatives.
Maintain a strong and visible presence at mine sites, strengthening customer relationships, supporting employees, and ensuring operational excellence across the region.

What You'll Bring

10+ years of progressive leadership experience within mining, heavy equipment, industrial, or related operational environments, including experience leading leaders.
Demonstrated success managing large-scale operations with accountability for safety, financial performance, workforce planning, and customer outcomes.
Strong operational knowledge across service, parts, supply chain, maintenance, and support functions, with the ability to lead cross-functional teams toward common goals.
Proven experience managing customer contracts, executing operational commitments, and building trusted relationships with key stakeholders.
Exceptional leadership, coaching, and talent development capabilities with a track record of building engaged, high-performing teams.
Strong business and financial acumen, including budgeting, forecasting, performance management, and strategic planning.
Excellent communication, relationship-building, problem-solving, and decision-making skills, with the ability to influence at all levels of the organization.
Previous mining industry experience and knowledge of heavy equipment operations, safety management systems, labour relations, and operational best practices are considered strong assets.

Comprehensive pension program with employer contributions
Employee Share Purchase Plan with company matching
Employer paid extended health, dental, and medical benefits available from day 1
This role is eligible for Finning’s Short Term Incentive Program
Competitive total rewards package designed to support your financial, physical, and personal well-being

Community. We value a sense of belonging, trusting each other, and encouraging authenticity. We contribute to our community.

Set and execute the North America Consumer strategy across the US and Canada, with clear plans to grow market share, revenue, customer value and profitability.

Partner with Global Pricing on pricing and FX margin strategies that balance adoption, competitiveness, revenue, margin and retention.

Customer Experience & Service Delivery

Lead consumer service and sales performance across Customer Success and Digital Sales, ensuring service and sales SLAs are consistently met or beaten.
Partner with Care leadership so the global Care function serves NAM customers well, meets service levels and resolves complaints quickly.
Use customer feedback, app reviews, NPS, service data and root-cause analysis to remove friction across the journey.

Operational & Cross-Functional Leadership

Work with global Revenue Operations and Sales Operations to align regional strategy, global programs, annual targets and performance reporting.
Partner with North America Compliance leadership so the Consumer business meets its US and Canadian regulatory obligations — including state money transmitter licensing, CFPB remittance rules, FinCEN, FINTRAC and Bank of Canada requirements — while keeping the experience fast and customer-centric.
Build, lead and develop a high-performing team and create clear cross-functional accountability across regional and global stakeholders.

Build and run a Consumer performance framework covering acquisition, conversion, activation, transactions, active customers, retention cohorts, revenue, profitability, CAC, LTV, channel performance, customer experience and product adoption.
Give senior leadership regular, insightful reporting that turns data into clear recommendations and actions.
Use data, customer insight and commercial analysis to guide investment decisions and close performance gaps.

Success in the role will be measured through a combination of commercial, customer and operational outcomes, including:

Growth in Consumer revenue, margin and market share across the US and Canada.

Volume, revenue and unit economics from new channels launched and scaled.

A digital-first operator who thinks in funnels, cohorts and experiments, and lives and breathes modern consumer apps.

new_jobs.description:
Description

At Xe, we live currencies
. Founded in 1993, Xe is a global leader in currency exchange and international money transfers. What began as a simple currency converter has grown into a platform trusted by over 300 million people each year. We provide a comprehensive range of currency services and products, including our real-time exchange rates, Currency Converter, Market Analysis and Currency Data API, supporting 130+ currencies across 190+ countries with quick, easy, secure Money Transfers for individuals and businesses. We leverage technology to deliver these services through our website, mobile app, and by phone. Backed by Euronet, we process more than $115 billion in global payments annually. Xe is profitable, product-led, and focused on building reliable, user-first tools that make moving money across borders easier for everyone.

Our Principles

At Xe, we value people who take initiative, think big, and follow through. We’re curious by nature and not afraid to ask what if or try something new. Everyone’s voice matters here. We expect people to speak up, bring ideas, and take ownership of their work. We don’t micromanage. We trust each other to make good calls, take responsibility, and move fast when it counts. And we care about community. Not in a vague corporate way, but in the sense that we have each other’s backs, stay open to feedback, and build a culture of trust and real collaboration.

Ambition. We dream big, try things out, and always ask “why not?” and “what if?” We’re ambitious in our thinking and our delivery.
Responsibility. We get involved, bring our perspective, and are always open to new ideas. We take personal responsibility.
Community. We value a sense of belonging, trusting each other, and encouraging authenticity. We contribute to our community.

The Role.
The Head of Consumer is the senior owner of Xe’s Consumer business in the United States and Canada, accountable for its strategy, proposition and commercial performance. Product, Marketing and Growth sit in global teams, so you will lead through influence: aligning them, along with Pricing, Sales, Customer Success, Care and Operations, behind the North America plan.

Responsibilities

This is a builder’s role. You will run the NAM Consumer business like a founder, owning revenue, profitability, acquisition, activation, retention, wallet share and customer lifetime value — and opening new channels to reach more customers. The role suits a digitally fluent leader with a background across product, marketing and growth in a fast-paced startup or scale-up. You know what great looks like in each function and can push global teams to deliver it for North American customers. Responsibilities include:

Consumer Strategy & Commercial Performance

Set and execute the North America Consumer strategy across the US and Canada, with clear plans to grow market share, revenue, customer value and profitability.
Own end-to-end commercial performance across the customer lifecycle: acquisition, activation, engagement, retention, wallet share and lifetime value.
Define the priorities, targets and operating rhythm for the Consumer business, and align regional and global stakeholders behind them.
Track a fast-moving competitive set — digital money transfer apps, neobanks, big tech wallets and incumbent banks — and spot new pockets of growth, such as high-value corridors and underserved diaspora communities.

Channel Expansion

Identify, build and scale new acquisition and distribution channels for Consumer in the US and Canada — for example, affiliate and referral programs, embedded and B2B2C distribution, community, diaspora and employer channels, and marketplaces.
Build the business case for each channel, run pilots, and scale those that hit CAC, volume and margin targets.
Lead commercial discussions with channel partners, including RFPs, and manage those relationships for ongoing performance.
Work with Compliance and Operations so each new channel launches safely and integrates cleanly into the customer journey.

Influencing Product, Marketing, Growth & Pricing

Be the voice of the NAM consumer with global Product, Marketing and Growth teams: bring market insight, set regional priorities, and secure roadmap and investment commitments.
Develop and own Customer Value Propositions for each Consumer segment in the US and Canada, and brief global teams on the features, benefits, pricing and service levels each segment needs.
Own regional go-to-market and in-market delivery of new products and propositions, coordinating cross-functional teams to maximize uptake and commercial return.
Champion test-and-learn on NAM funnels, onboarding and messaging, and hold partner teams to agreed outcomes.
Partner with Global Pricing on pricing and FX margin strategies that balance adoption, competitiveness, revenue, margin and retention.

Customer Experience & Service Delivery

Lead consumer service and sales performance across Customer Success and Digital Sales, ensuring service and sales SLAs are consistently met or beaten.
Partner with Care leadership so the global Care function serves NAM customers well, meets service levels and resolves complaints quickly.
Use customer feedback, app reviews, NPS, service data and root-cause analysis to remove friction across the journey.

Operational & Cross-Functional Leadership

Work with global Revenue Operations and Sales Operations to align regional strategy, global programs, annual targets and performance reporting.
Partner with North America Compliance leadership so the Consumer business meets its US and Canadian regulatory obligations — including state money transmitter licensing, CFPB remittance rules, FinCEN, FINTRAC and Bank of Canada requirements — while keeping the experience fast and customer-centric.
Build, lead and develop a high-performing team and create clear cross-functional accountability across regional and global stakeholders.

Performance Management & Reporting

Build and run a Consumer performance framework covering acquisition, conversion, activation, transactions, active customers, retention cohorts, revenue, profitability, CAC, LTV, channel performance, customer experience and product adoption.
Give senior leadership regular, insightful reporting that turns data into clear recommendations and actions.
Use data, customer insight and commercial analysis to guide investment decisions and close performance gaps.

How Success is Measured.
Success in the role will be measured through a combination of commercial, customer and operational outcomes, including:

Growth in Consumer revenue, margin and market share across the US and Canada.
Growth in active Consumer customers and transaction volumes.
Volume, revenue and unit economics from new channels launched and scaled.
Improved acquisition, conversion and activation, from sign-up to first transfer.
Increased retention, repeat usage and wallet share.
Adoption and commercial performance of new products and propositions in NAM.
Improved customer experience and service performance (e.g. NPS, app ratings, SLAs).
Stronger cross-functional execution and delivery of NAM priorities by global teams.

What You Bring

A digital-first operator who thinks in funnels, cohorts and experiments, and lives and breathes modern consumer apps.
Hands-on leadership experience across Product, Marketing and Growth — ideally having owned or run more than one of these functions.
A track record in a high-growth, fast-paced startup or scale-up environment, ideally in consumer fintech, payments, money transfer, neobanking or another digital consumer business.
Proven results scaling a consumer product: driving acquisition, activation, retention and monetization with measurable impact.
Fluency with the modern growth stack — product analytics, experimentation platforms, CRM and lifecycle tools, attribution and paid acquisition channels.
Strong commercial and analytical skills, with a firm grasp of unit economics (CAC, LTV, payback, contribution margin) and data-driven decision-making.
Experience building and leading high-performing, cross-functional teams, and comfort influencing in a matrixed global organization.
A bias for action: you move fast, ship, learn and iterate, while keeping the bigger strategic picture in view.
Excellent communication and storytelling, from team stand-ups to senior leadership.
